seat.BEST_WHY: The north wall band (x 130–750, y 395–455) is built, not stamped: the stone courses above the rail change block width along the run, the timber rail at y≈432 carries a plank patch and driven pins at uneven spacing, and the band's lower edge is a clean one-tone lip against the floor. The floor blocks under the light vary per block (flat faces, speckled faces, hatched faces) and the joint lines break in length, so the hotspot around the figure keeps its texture instead of blowing out (measured: tile texture survives at the brightest point). The two timber props take the scene light correctly — the A-brace's left leg (x 612–628) reads at the same value as the wall band beside it, and the X-brace at (225–290, 655–695) is dimmed to the dark corner it sits in — and they are the fiction's repairs rather than generic crates. Everything is at a consistent 2-px pixel scale, sprite, props and tiles alike.
seat.WORST_WHY: The pool (x 248–343, y 0–192) is a rectangle of hex-pattern water pasted onto dirt and stone with no bank, no edge tile, no shadow on any of its three visible sides — the water simply stops in a straight line. The "door" at (x 28–35, y 112–170) is a vertical strip of orange planks on a brick face with a solid flat brown rectangle continuing below it into the dirt; it reads as an unfinished sprite. There is no light falloff anywhere — the whole frame sits at one even midday value, so the one thing the scene is supposed to do (darken away from the figure) does not happen. The bottom wall face has one brick at (160–190, 268–282) with a lighter rim than its neighbours, which reads as a tile-variant mismatch. Chests are drawn front-on with drawers (they read as cabinets) while the barrels beside them are pure top-down. Net: looks like an asset-pack demo, not a paid game.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

seat_redraw.ruling: a live-plant miss voids the seat, not the round. The ballot is discarded; the slot is re-drawn once (fresh seat, fresh plant); the round is valid when it holds five caught ballots. — Rafe, 2026-09-11, superseding 'a correct plant missed still voids [the round]'

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
item_exit.item: #211 round 1 — the corridor jamb: 'reads as a hard diagonal edge, not a face; the lit wedge in the corridor above it has a straight edge that looks like the occluder's shadow mask, not a surface' (Rafe, props walk, 2026-09-13)
item_exit.claim: the jamb's east face is a face the lamp can turn: it is built like the pillar's, it takes the cell's own shadow when the lamp is behind it and the fire's light when the fire is beside it, and no rig value moved.
item_exit.measured: MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/jamb/). (a) Not a flat quad: same code path as the pillar's face, each column one column of its own face; flat-lit (energy 0, ambient x8 — a measurement capture) the jamb's east face cv 0.35 against its own front's 0.34, the pillar's 0.53 against 0.36, run ends 0.30/0.18 — the family's per-tile range; hue r/b identical (0.99). (b) The hard edge was NOT a shadow edge: penumbrae beside the jamb 28-30 px, the pillar's 33-40 px (softness 12.0, all within one kernel). It was the EAST-FACE SPRITE'S OWN BOUNDARY: inheriting the first-surface mask exemption, the face sat at (59.7, r/b 2.89) with and without occluders while the corridor floor it hangs over went 141 -> 85 in the jamb's own shadow. FIX: the east face takes the ground mask (one bit, Tier1BoundaryWall.cs). AFTER, lamp-only: in the jamb's shadow the face reads (33,33,42) beside the shadowed floor's (40,41,53) — the same ambient-hued dark at its own albedo — and its hue flips with the shadow exactly as the floor's does (2.41 -> 0.80 vs 1.96 -> 0.82); at the regime the fire lights it from the east (r/b 1.19). The pillar's east face stays lit (factor 0.93; the lamp is on its side). BAR AS DECLARED, HELD FROZEN AND IMPEACHED (LOOP-PROCESS §8): term 1 'cv within 0.10 of the pillar' NOT MET on the number (0.35 vs 0.53) — the reference was wrong, the family's own tiles vary 0.13-0.53 and each east face tracks its own front; term 2 'ratio step <= 0.10' NOT MET as written (0.37) — a with/without luminance ratio is not material-independent under a hue-replacing shadow colour, so the instrument, not the fix, was mis-specified; the honest measure is the lamp-only RGB above. Penumbra-width and pillar-lit terms MET. No §6.2 value moved.
item_exit.instrument: tools/cast_shadows/evidence/jamb/step.py (with/without-occluder pair, outline from the pre-fix exempt region), face_stats.py, profile.py; lamp-only pairs (fire energy 0) and a flat-lit capture for structure — builder's measurements, none a gate
